headline: Highest risk is medium: AutoGPT can write files and use allowlisted network egress, while the paired repo is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, so interaction risks are limited but not absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and write the filesystem and call agent protocol APIs, so if the operator manually bridges its outputs into the other repo, prompt-like content could be misread. The awesome-production-machine-learning repo is non-runnable and exposes no I/O surfaces, so there is no default automated bridge; the pathway is unusual and limited.
conditions: IF the operator copies AutoGPT output into files later consumed by the other repo
IF a shared filesystem is used as a manual handoff channel
mitigations: Keep the repos in separate directories
Review any file content before reusing it
Use read-only mounts for the non-runnable repo

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted egress, but the paired repo has no declared I/O surfaces and no data classes touched. With no shared workspace or sensitive data indicated, leakage is not a default pathway; any exposure would require an operator-created bridge.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace
IF sensitive files are placed in AutoGPT's accessible filesystem
mitigations: Store sensitive files outside AutoGPT's working directory
Use separate OS users for each agent
Restrict AutoGPT to a minimal allowlist

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem; the other repo is non-runnable but still represents a shared mutable workspace if colocated. The conflict is not high because B lacks write capabilities, yet overlapping filesystem access can still cause accidental overwrites or state drift.
conditions: IF both agents are given write access to the same directory
IF AutoGPT is allowed to modify files that the other repo also uses
mitigations: Disable AutoGPT file writes for shared paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate outputs from files and APIs, and the other repo is a curated resource that could be treated as authoritative by an operator or downstream workflow. Because B is non-runnable, the cascade is indirect, but if A's output is reused without verification, errors can propagate into documentation or decisions.
conditions: IF AutoGPT output is copied into downstream notes or automation
IF the downstream process treats the curated repo as authoritative without checking provenance
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs
Add provenance labels to copied content
Avoid auto-importing A outputs into B-linked workflows

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes, residency constraints, or regulated scopes are declared for either agent, and B is non-runnable. With no PHI, EU PII, or retention mismatch evidence, there is no compliance pathway to score beyond none.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later introduced into either agent
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both repos
Reassess if residency or retention requirements change
